ledger.title: Ledger
ledger.head: Head hash
ledger.intact: Chain intact — {count} entries re-derived from their canonical form.
ledger.explain: Verification recomputes every entry hash from the recorded metadata and checks that each entry links to its predecessor. It reads the whole chain rather than a sample.
ledger.anchorExplain: Scheduled anchoring runs hourly and covers complete UTC days, so a token from a qualified authority costs one request per day rather than one per snapshot. Anchoring now covers everything pending, including captures from today — use it when you need an evidence package before tomorrow.
ledger.anchored: Anchored {count} entries. The authority attested them at {time}.
ledger.nothingPending: Nothing pending — every entry is already anchored.

storage.label: Storage immutability
storage.Enforced: Enforced — a deletion under retention was refused
storage.note: Proof rests on the hash chain and the external timestamp, both of which survive the storage being wiped. Object Lock is defence in depth.

timestamp.unqualifiedWarning: Timestamps are coming from a demonstration service. They are technically valid and verifiable, but will not carry a legal dispute. Configure a qualified provider before capturing anything you may need to rely on.

snapshot.title: Snapshot
snapshot.evidenceHint: A ZIP containing the archive, the protocol, the timestamp token and a verification script the other side can run themselves.
snapshot.notTimestamped: This snapshot has not been anchored yet. Anchoring runs once a day; an evidence package exported before then could not be verified independently.
snapshot.payloadHint: What the endpoint returned, stored byte for byte. The hash above covers exactly these bytes.
snapshot.payloadNotShown: This payload is {type} and is not shown here. Download it to inspect it.
snapshot.pluginSourceHint: The configuration below is part of the entry hash and ships with the evidence package.

projects.title: Projects
projects.queued: Capture queued for “{name}”. The worker picks it up shortly; the first run also pulls the crawler image, so it can take a few minutes.

form.name: Name
form.seedUrlsHint: One per line. These are the pages the crawl starts from.
form.scopeHint: URL prefixes, one per line. Leave empty to capture only the seed URLs themselves. Archiving sites that are not yours is technically identical and legally a different question — crawl politely and take advice first.
form.scheduleHint: Cron expression, evaluated in UTC. Empty means on demand only. Example: 0 3 * * * is daily at 03:00 UTC.
form.retentionWarning: Can be extended later, never shortened.
form.profileHint: Fixes the browser settings for every capture in this project, and is named in every evidence package.
form.needSeed: At least one seed URL is required.

plugins.title: Capture plugins
plugins.intro: A capture plugin archives something the page alone does not contain — for example the prices your own systems quoted at the moment the page was captured. Its output becomes a snapshot in the same chain, under the same daily timestamp, and can be verified from an evidence package the same way.
plugins.name: Name
plugins.newBindingHint: Saving creates a new version and supersedes the previous one. Nothing is overwritten.
plugins.configurationHint: JSON, stored exactly as written. It is hashed into the entry and shipped in every evidence package, so it must not contain credentials.
plugins.secretRefHint: Name of an environment variable on the worker, e.g. PS_SECRET_ERP_TOKEN. The name is recorded; the value is never stored.
plugins.rationaleHint: Shown in the evidence package, like the rationale on a capture profile.
plugins.requiredHint: Off by default. A page capture cannot be taken again later, so an unreachable endpoint should not cost you one. The failure is recorded on the run either way.
plugins.noneLive: No plugin is bound to a project.
plugins.historyHint: Kept so that a snapshot can always name the configuration it ran under. Nothing here is deleted.
plugins.noneInstalled: This build contains no capture plugins
plugins.noneInstalledDetail: Plugins are compiled in rather than loaded at runtime, so that the code which produced a piece of evidence is always the published source.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.subject: Subject
audit.note: Reads are recorded here as well as writes. Entries cannot be edited or deleted.

auth.signInHint: This archive is not public. Access is recorded against your account.
auth.setupHint: No account exists yet. The one you create here becomes the first user; afterwards, only a signed-in user can add further accounts.
auth.badCredentials: That email and password combination was not accepted.
auth.accessLogged: Viewing a snapshot, replaying an archive and exporting an evidence package are all recorded in the audit log against the account that did them.
